components.name: Inexact inverse Hessian action
components.operation: At the approximate inner point solve H_k q_k=a_k to certified residual epsilon_k, then form c_k-B_k^Tq_k.
components.requires: Both the inner distance certificate and the linear residual certificate; for the linked bound, all conditions in thm.P051.direction_error.
transfer_checks: Re-establish the relation between an implementable inner stopping rule and distance to the same selected branch.
Check invertibility and conditioning at approximate points; A2 states invertibility at exact branch points.
Conjugate gradient is mentioned by the source as a practical implementation, but a generic nonsingular Hessian need not be positive definite; do not assert a CG convergence guarantee from A2 alone.

variants.cost: Charge inner-solver work separately from linear-system work. Each linear iteration may consume Hessian-vector products; checking its residual requires forming H_k q_k-a_k or an equivalent certified solver quantity. Separately charge evaluation of ∇_1g and ∇_2g and the mixed-derivative transpose action B_k^Tq_k. Explicit Hessian formation/factorization, if used, is additional work. The source supplies no universal count of these operations as a function of epsilon_k under A1–A3. A distance certificate is required rather than treated as a free available Oracle. The direction component performs no projection; a caller using Algorithm 1(iv) must additionally charge projection and outer-iteration work.
variants.implementation_details_ref: PDF page 3 Algorithm 1(i)–(iii) and following access discussion; page 4 opening Hessian-vector product paragraph. Page 5 implementation heuristics are not included in the certified component.
variants.name: Algorithm 1 direction component, steps (i)–(iii)
variants.output: The vector p_k in R^s. No averaging, random selection or restriction on its coordinate support is specified.
public_inputs: lambda_k in D subset R^s and epsilon_k>0
Functions h:R^p×R^s→R and g:R^p×R^s→R, selected inner solution X(lambda_k), or an inner solver with a valid distance certificate
Access to ∇_1g, ∇_2g, H=∇²_11h and the transpose mixed-derivative action B^Tq for B=∇²_12h
variants.query_and_update: (i) Call the inner solver to produce x_k with ||X(lambda_k)-x_k||≤epsilon_k. (ii) Evaluate a_k=∇_1g(x_k,lambda_k) and solve H_k q_k=a_k approximately until ||H_k q_k-a_k||≤epsilon_k, where H_k=∇²_11h(x_k,lambda_k). (iii) Evaluate c_k=∇_2g(x_k,lambda_k) and B_k^Tq_k, where B_k=∇²_12h(x_k,lambda_k), and return p_k=c_k-B_k^Tq_k. All derivatives here use the approximate x_k, not the exact X(lambda_k).
variants.requirements: An inner approximation with ||x_k-X(lambda_k)||≤epsilon_k must be obtainable. At (x_k,lambda_k), the linear system H_k q=a_k must admit a solution meeting the residual tolerance, and a_k,c_k,B_k^Tq must be evaluable. The linked error lemma additionally requires its explicit smooth branch, compact domain, nonsingular exact Hessians and uniform derivative conditions; those are performance conditions, not an assertion that every call to the formula has a certified error.
variants.state_and_initialization: For one direction call take lambda_k and epsilon_k as inputs; there is no persistent direction state and no prescribed x or q initialization. The inner and linear solvers may choose their own initial points but must meet the two certificates. x_k,q_k are in R^p and p_k is in R^s. Repeated calls in Algorithm 1 may start at a user-supplied lambda_1 in D; the displayed Algorithm 1 does not prescribe a universal initialization.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Stop the two internal solves only when their respective distance and residual certificates hold at the supplied epsilon_k. For the linked eventual direction-error bound take epsilon_k→0. Summability is not needed by that direction lemma. This component does not choose an outer stopping criterion or step size. For context, source Algorithm 1(iv) separately uses lambda_(k+1)=P_D(lambda_k-p_k/L); that outer update and Theorem 2 convergence are not this component's performance claim.
